scope: Declarative real-PostgreSQL acceptance matrix for a future atomic admission transaction and recovery boundary; no executable harness, migration, connection, credentials, publication, media processing, or cloud action.

governance.current_evidence: E1: local SQL source inspection and synthetic JSON; no PostgreSQL E2/E3 proof
governance.independent_assurance: NOT_RUN; I2 or higher required before adopting the production design

prerequisites.requirement: Future server functions absent: video_queue.admit_approved_subset(uuid,text,text,text,uuid) and video_queue.recover_subset_admission(text,text,text). This plan does not implement them.

Implement server-owned subset_approval containing the complete approved contract and exact queue manifest, subset_admission immutable header/binding, source_reservation global primary key google_drive:<file_id>, and trusted source_observation. Caller hashes alone are not approval or observation evidence.

Reuse the existing request-key transaction lock. Recover an exact committed binding or return legacy/conflict HOLD before freshness checks or new reservations. For a new admission, lock approval and trusted observation, INSERT a transient admission draft, then reserve ALL exact source_identity keys through the immediate primary key in canonical COLLATE C insertion order, including initially absent keys. All reservation/unique-index waits finish BEFORE the final clock_timestamp freshness/authorization check. SELECT FOR UPDATE alone cannot lock absent source keys. If INSERT ON CONFLICT does not insert, read the owner in a separate READ COMMITTED statement with a new snapshot; never rely on a stale single-CTE fallback lookup. Conflicts are explicit; no silent skipping/filtering. Only after this gate invoke existing enqueue_drive_batch in the SAME transaction, verify exact actual jobs and persist the complete immutable binding. Any exception rolls all drafts/reservations/enqueue/consumption/binding writes back. No new source advisory-lock namespace.

Revoke legacy app EXECUTE on enqueue_drive_batch, protect all base-table DML, and install triggers requiring persisted trusted reservation/approval linkage and immutable identity. No session GUC, custom setting, caller role name, client boolean, checksum, or caller-provided timestamp may authorize insertion.

Cutover must stop/drain every legacy and new writer, wait for earlier writer transactions, backfill permanent tombstones for every historical source from all job statuses, preserve duplicate history provenance, install guards and revocations before reopening. Unknown history or an active legacy writer keeps cutover blocked.

Future worker server boundary checks trusted source observation tied to contract, job UUID, non-null lease token, exact attempt, worker, server timestamp and nonce immediately before processing every attempt. A claim alone is not media-processing permission. Retry/reclaim/claim enforce a server maximum of three attempts independent of caller p_max_attempts. Legacy worker credentials must not claim managed rows after commit. The existing claim selector needs an eligibility predicate for finalized authorized rollout rows, avoiding claim-then-rollback starvation. Prevent attempt_count decrease/reset.

Use an explicitly provisioned disposable PostgreSQL database only, with pgcrypto, required base roles, migrations 0056,0057,0058 including both subfiles, optional 0059, and the reviewed FUTURE admission migration. Pin PostgreSQL version, migration checksums and role ACLs in evidence. No DSN is embedded or inferred by this JSON.

Future test support under admission_test is not implemented here. It seeds synthetic server-owned approvals/observations as a privileged fixture principal; supplies deterministic failpoints/barriers; maps invoke_attempt_gate to the ACTUAL future worker server boundary without replacing it by a Python fake. Its helper SQL is a design dependency, not a production API.

Per-case fresh disposable state; actual independent PostgreSQL connections and roles. The coordinator uses barriers/pg_blocking_pids to prove interleaving rather than relying on thread scheduling or sleeps. Set finite statement/lock timeouts. Capture query results, SQLSTATE, constraint names, backend IDs and commit acknowledgements.

JSON parsing/static checks may run under bare pytest without any DB/network. No pytest import/collection hook, autouse fixture or DSN environment lookup may run this SQL; no executable test harness is part of this change. A separately authorized future integration runner must fail closed when any prerequisite is absent.

design_contract.admission_signature: video_queue.admit_approved_subset(p_approval_id uuid,p_request_key text,p_contract_sha256 text,p_queue_manifest_sha256 text,p_observation_id uuid) RETURNS jsonb
design_contract.admission_success: Exact rich persisted_binding_contract JSON only, including embedded binding_sha256; never the lease compatibility projection or mutable progress fields.
design_contract.recovery_success: Return precisely the persisted immutable binding; do not call enqueue, refresh source metadata, require original observation freshness, or compare mutable status as immutable identity.

recovery_not_found.when: No header, queue row, reservation or historical request evidence exists. Observation and approval still required for a separate admission call.

recovery_hold.when: Legacy/unbound request, mismatched caller digests, incomplete/corrupt mapping, uncertain historical provenance or partial state. No re-enqueue or repair on read.

design_contract.error_status: Proposed stable VIDEO_ADMISSION_* design codes below are expected semantics, not implemented or observed PostgreSQL results. Existing VIDEO_QUEUE_* names are quoted from checked-in SQL. Capture actual SQLSTATE as well; unspecified future SQLSTATE must be frozen before execution.
design_contract.reservation_policy: source_identity PRIMARY KEY equals google_drive:<file_id>. Committed reservations and HISTORICAL_HOLD tombstones cannot be released, deleted, reassigned or replaced on failure, retry, canary review, source revision/name change or a new request key.
design_contract.observation_policy: Rows, scope, timestamp and nonce are issued by the trusted collector. Verify exact source set and approved name/revision/fingerprint. At the final locked authorization point AFTER all lock waits require observed_at <= clock_timestamp() AND clock_timestamp() < expires_at, with 0 < expires_at-observed_at <= 30 seconds. The envelope begins at the oldest constituent read. This is not an absolute COMMIT-time freshness guarantee: SET CONSTRAINTS ALL IMMEDIATE followed by idle can make the evidence stale before COMMIT. The trusted caller owns the outer transaction, commits once promptly and exposes the receipt only after successful COMMIT. Fresh trusted observation and lease checks remain mandatory before every processing attempt. Caller payloads/GUCs cannot establish trust.

persisted_binding_contract.job_order: Ascending exact queue-manifest sequence; unique actual job_id and file_id; bijection with all actual jobs and permanent reservations of the admitted batch.
persisted_binding_contract.digest_rule: binding_sha256 = SHA256(canonical UTF-8 JSON of every exact top-level field except binding_sha256); header digest equals embedded binding_sha256.
persisted_binding_contract.note: This full rich shape is the persisted binding returned by admission/recovery. project_lease_binding produces a separate five-key compatibility projection only after complete rich binding revalidation.

lease_binding_projection.purpose: Existing subset_contract.check_attempt compatibility only, after full rich immutable binding revalidation.

design_contract.proposed_column_semantics: Names describe absent future schema, not implemented DDL. Approval stores verified canonical contract/manifest bytes and parsed data, hashes, trusted approver/plan/capture provenance and mutable expiry/revocation authorization. Admission stores immutable plan/subset/contract/manifest hashes and exact rich binding bytes/hash/commit receipt. ADMITTED reservations retain immutable request/admission, approved source_fingerprint and actual batch_id/job_id; HISTORICAL_HOLD instead preserves provenance to all historical jobs and never fabricates an approved fingerprint or managed mapping. Observation sources retain exact native metadata/fingerprint records, oldest constituent server timestamp, scope and trusted collector provenance.

sequence: Existing request-key lock; committed immutable recovery or legacy HOLD before freshness/reservations.
Lock and validate server approval and trusted observation authority/scope.
INSERT transient admission draft in the same transaction.
INSERT ALL exact source_identity reservations in ascending COLLATE C order; immediate PK handles both existing and absent keys.
Resolve every reservation wait and conflict; then perform the final locked clock_timestamp freshness/authorization check.
Nested existing enqueue, exact actual job mapping, rich binding finalization and structural validation; one outer COMMIT.
reservation_acquisition.absent_key_rule: SELECT FOR UPDATE on source_reservation is insufficient for an absent key. Immediate PK insertion establishes exclusion; no extra source advisory-lock namespace is proposed.
reservation_acquisition.conflict_rule: A different committed owner or HISTORICAL_HOLD is an explicit conflict, never an omitted source. If a conflicting transaction rolls back, the waiting insert may acquire the key, but it must still pass the final freshness gate after that wait.
reservation_acquisition.conflict_snapshot_rule: At READ COMMITTED, an INSERT ON CONFLICT outcome may observe a conflicting row not visible to that statement snapshot. Owner lookup therefore uses a separate subsequent SQL statement/new snapshot, not an INSERT+SELECT fallback in one stale CTE. Missing/inconsistent owner evidence fails closed; no blind enqueue.

conflict_owner_lookup.sql: SELECT admission_id,request_key,reservation_kind FROM video_queue.source_reservation WHERE source_identity=$1::text;
conflict_owner_lookup.expected: Run as a separate READ COMMITTED statement after the INSERT conflict has resolved; exact owner/tombstone, or fail closed if ownership cannot be established.

B_overlap.purpose: different contract and deterministic request key, shared source 1

R_reverse.purpose: different approved contract/key; synthetic names chosen so pure queue normalization is exactly [2,1]

fixture_data.construction: Future privileged fixture setup builds full canonical contracts from the synthetic raw rows with the existing PURE batch_plan.build_batch_plan and subset_contract.build_subset_contract, stores full_contract and exact enqueue_manifest in subset_approval, and recomputes every hash on the server. R_reverse changes synthetic display names before building, never blindly reverses a hashed manifest. Fixture seed support must not create an approval from only caller digests.
fixture_data.parameter_binding: $1..$N are typed parameters resolved by the future runner from named synthetic fixtures/captured SQL results. They are not psql variables, shell substitutions, real IDs or unresolved SQL literals.

additional_symbolic_fixtures.invalid_approval_variant: Each deliberately malformed privileged approval fixture in G05; retain explicit generated approval_id,request_key,contract_sha256,queue_manifest_sha256,observation_id.
additional_symbolic_fixtures.historical_source_readmission_variant: Fresh valid full approved contract/manifest using historical source 1 with changed revision/profile/key; explicitly generated five admission arguments.
additional_symbolic_fixtures.changed_source_readmission_variant: Fresh valid full approved contract/manifest still using already reserved source 1 after source changes; explicitly generated five admission arguments.
additional_symbolic_fixtures.legacy_overlap_fixture: Pre-cutover synthetic legacy key distinct from A, exact A folders/profile/revision and one-source-1 manifest; nine explicit enqueue fields including canonical files inventory digest.
additional_symbolic_fixtures.legacy_inflight_fixture: Synthetic historical legacy request held during cutover; same one-source-1 metadata and all nine explicit enqueue fields.
additional_symbolic_fixtures.legacy_recovery_fixture: Legacy existing request key and explicit claimed contract/manifest hashes; absence of committed rich binding must return HOLD even when both hashes are supplied.
additional_symbolic_fixtures.damaged_binding_variant: Each independently seeded corrupt binding fixture; exact request key and caller contract/manifest hashes preserved from the undamaged committed fixture.
additional_symbolic_fixtures.invalid_observation_variant: Each invalid observation UUID in S08. Missing-row case uses a deliberately absent UUID; other variants refer to separately seeded rows. No synthesized trust.
additional_symbolic_fixtures.A.refreshed_observation_id: Captured from the fresh trusted observation SQL only after the failed transaction snapshot and unconsumed-observation assertions have succeeded.

ADMIN.purpose: privileged setup and invariant inspection only; never represents the application

LEGACY.purpose: existing legacy enqueue caller, revoked after cutover

WORKER.purpose: dedicated authenticated upgraded worker; old credentials cannot assume this role

COLLECTOR.purpose: persist synthetic trusted observation through fixture adapter

ATTACKER.purpose: no privileged memberships, owner, superuser or BYPASSRLS

GUARDED_WRITER.purpose: test-only limited job DML grant, not owner/superuser; verifies triggers still reject even if a routine DML privilege is accidentally granted

OLD_WORKER.purpose: actual old credential identity; must not claim or mutate managed jobs even after commit

execution_protocol.isolation: READ COMMITTED required baseline. Repeat concurrency groups at SERIALIZABLE; bounded 40001 retry must retry the whole transaction and preserve at-most-one binding. 40P01 deadlock is a test failure for reversed-order case.
execution_protocol.barrier_policy: Use coordinator-controlled test-only failpoint instrumentation around real production statements. The coordinator holds advisory locks; instrumented sessions emit reached events then wait on those locks. Hooks cannot bypass auth/constraints or commit nested work and must be absent from production. No fake queue, mutex-only model, GUC trust or arbitrary sleep counts as evidence.
barrier_helper_signatures_absent: admission_test.invoke_attempt_gate(job_id uuid,lease_token uuid,worker_key text,attempt_count integer,observation_id uuid) RETURNS jsonb
execution_protocol.session_identification_sql: SELECT pg_backend_pid() AS backend_pid, session_user, current_user;
execution_protocol.wait_evidence_sql: SELECT pid,wait_event_type,wait_event,pg_blocking_pids(pid) AS blockers FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE pid=ANY($1::integer[]);
execution_protocol.snapshots: Use snapshot SQL in assertions, capture before and after rejection/rollback. Exclude sequence counters and external statement telemetry from atomicity assertions; PostgreSQL sequences need not roll back. Include batch/job/event/admission/reservation persisted row data, not aggregate counts alone.
execution_protocol.cleanup: Discard only the explicitly provisioned disposable database through its separately authorized lifecycle; no production cleanup SQL or connection provided here.
execution_protocol.result_capture: Each case remains NOT_RUN until real PostgreSQL evidence contains version, migration hashes, role, statement, parameters provenance, actual results/errors, barrier proof and invariant snapshots.
execution_protocol.fixture_helper_rule: Any admission_test helper is absent/unimplemented planning notation. It may orchestrate or seed a disposable test but MUST call or inspect the real production boundary. A helper that simulates admission, retry, source authorization, cutover or locks cannot count as PostgreSQL proof.
execution_protocol.session_step_rule: Setup states are established before the listed schedule. Steps with dispatch=async are sent without blocking the coordinator; dependent COMMIT waits for the paused statement result after the named barrier is released. Error statements use savepoints/subtransactions or end with ROLLBACK before the next independent variant. Each variant executes in a fresh seeded database state.
execution_protocol.parameter_expansion_rule: All SQL steps list one explicit symbolic parameter reference per positional $n. No wildcard expansion or prose parameter packing is permitted. Fixture producers must resolve every symbolic field and verify its type before any future integration run; unresolved fixture data is a prerequisite failure, not a default. Signature positions are admission [approval_id,request_key,contract_sha256,queue_manifest_sha256,observation_id], recovery [request_key,contract_sha256,queue_manifest_sha256], legacy enqueue [request_key,source_folder_id,output_folder_id,work_folder_id,processing_profile,algorithm_revision,canary_source_file_id,inventory_sha256,files].
execution_protocol.freshness_limit: Deferred structural constraints enforce complete binding; they cannot guarantee freshness at every COMMIT. SET CONSTRAINTS ALL IMMEDIATE may fire a deferred trigger while evidence is fresh and leave no pending check after an idle period. Authorization freshness is checked at the final locked authorization point. The test plan documents this limit instead of promising unconditional stale-COMMIT rejection.
execution_protocol.deferred_commit_rule: Admission SQL functions cannot commit. The trusted thin caller owns the outer transaction, commits once and exposes the binding only after COMMIT. Deferred checks enforce structural completeness. Their timing is not a guaranteed final clock check if a caller forces them immediate; a later attempt requires new source/lease evidence.

known_current_gaps.finding: Request-key advisory lock prevents same-key duplicate inserts only. No global cross-batch source uniqueness or persisted approval/reservation exists.
Existing request compares inventory hash, count and aggregate metadata; it does not prove exact stored job rows equal the approved manifest.
p_max_attempts permits 1..10; attempt 3 with max_attempts=4 requeues, and claim_job has no attempt cap for QUEUED rows. A fourth normal retry is therefore possible.
lease_token <> p_lease_token permits SQL UNKNOWN for null token when all other terms are false. Proposed guard must reject null explicitly; heartbeat and SQL0058 finish have different predicates.
The fake uses terminal receipt /v2 and incomplete artifact objects, whereas SQL0058 requires receipt /v1, full source identity, flags, locators, positive sizes, revisions and binding hashes.
Python lock/rollback model is not PostgreSQL concurrency, ACL or trigger evidence; source/status-dependent recovery there is unsuitable for immutable committed binding recovery.
NOT VALID exempts old rows from initial scan but checks new/updated REVIEW_READY rows.
0058 requires positive numeric artifact sizes; 0059 adds integral values and upper bounds. Do not attribute 0059 limits to 0058.

unique_request_header.sql: SELECT count(*) = 1 AS ok FROM video_queue.subset_admission WHERE request_key=$1::text;

single_batch.sql: SELECT count(*)=1 AS ok FROM video_queue.batch WHERE request_key=$1::text;

no_global_duplicate_reservation.sql: SELECT NOT EXISTS(SELECT source_identity FROM video_queue.source_reservation GROUP BY source_identity HAVING count(*)>1) AS ok;

reservations_exact.sql: SELECT array_agg(r.source_identity ORDER BY r.source_identity) = $2::text[] AS ok FROM video_queue.source_reservation r JOIN video_queue.subset_admission a ON a.admission_id=r.admission_id WHERE a.request_key=$1::text;

exact_jobs_not_just_count.sql: WITH approved AS (SELECT (f->>'sequence')::integer AS sequence,f->>'file_id' AS file_id,f->>'name' AS name,f->>'mime_type' AS mime_type,(f->>'size_bytes')::bigint AS size_bytes,f->>'checksum' AS checksum FROM video_queue.subset_approval a CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(a.queue_manifest->'files') f WHERE a.approval_id=$1::uuid), actual AS (SELECT j.sequence,j.source_file_id AS file_id,j.source_name AS name,j.source_mime_type AS mime_type,j.source_size_bytes AS size_bytes,j.source_checksum AS checksum FROM video_queue.job j JOIN video_queue.batch b USING(batch_id) WHERE b.request_key=$2::text) SELECT NOT EXISTS((SELECT * FROM approved EXCEPT SELECT * FROM actual) UNION ALL (SELECT * FROM actual EXCEPT SELECT * FROM approved)) AS ok;

binding_maps_real_jobs.sql: WITH h AS (SELECT * FROM video_queue.subset_admission WHERE request_key=$1::text), mapped AS (SELECT (x->>'job_id')::uuid AS job_id,x->>'file_id' AS file_id,(x->>'sequence')::integer AS sequence,x->>'source_identity' AS source_identity,x->>'source_fingerprint' AS source_fingerprint FROM h CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(h.binding->'jobs') x), actual AS (SELECT j.job_id,j.source_file_id AS file_id,j.sequence,'google_drive:'||j.source_file_id AS source_identity,f->>'source_fingerprint' AS source_fingerprint FROM video_queue.job j JOIN h ON h.batch_id=j.batch_id JOIN video_queue.subset_approval p ON p.approval_id=h.approval_id CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(p.full_contract->'files') f WHERE f->>'file_id'=j.source_file_id), reserved AS (SELECT r.job_id,j.source_file_id AS file_id,j.sequence,r.source_identity,r.source_fingerprint FROM video_queue.source_reservation r JOIN h ON h.admission_id=r.admission_id AND h.request_key=r.request_key AND h.batch_id=r.batch_id JOIN video_queue.job j ON j.job_id=r.job_id AND j.batch_id=r.batch_id AND r.source_identity='google_drive:'||j.source_file_id) SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM h)=1 AND (SELECT count(*) FROM actual)>0 AND NOT EXISTS((SELECT * FROM mapped EXCEPT SELECT * FROM actual) UNION ALL (SELECT * FROM actual EXCEPT SELECT * FROM mapped) UNION ALL (SELECT * FROM mapped EXCEPT SELECT * FROM reserved) UNION ALL (SELECT * FROM reserved EXCEPT SELECT * FROM mapped)) AND (SELECT count(*) FROM mapped)=(SELECT count(DISTINCT job_id) FROM mapped) AND (SELECT count(*) FROM mapped)=(SELECT count(DISTINCT file_id) FROM mapped) AND (SELECT count(*) FROM actual)=(SELECT count(*) FROM video_queue.job j JOIN h ON h.batch_id=j.batch_id) AS ok;
binding_maps_real_jobs.scope: Compare each rich binding entry against the actual queue job, full approved source fingerprint and permanent reservation mapping; the five-key lease projection is not sufficient evidence.

binding_hash.sql: SELECT a.binding_sha256 IS NOT NULL AND a.binding_sha256 = a.binding->>'binding_sha256' AND a.binding_sha256 = encode(public.digest(convert_to(video_queue.canonical_json_text(a.binding - 'binding_sha256'),'UTF8'),'sha256'),'hex') AS ok FROM video_queue.subset_admission a WHERE a.request_key=$1::text;
binding_hash.codec_note: Matches admission_binding.build_binding: hash the rich binding core with binding_sha256 excluded, then require both the header digest and embedded digest to equal that hash. This canonical_json_text SQL is a proposed check; cross-runtime canonicalization vectors must pass before activation.

immutable_snapshot.sql: SELECT jsonb_build_object('header',jsonb_build_object('admission_id',a.admission_id,'approval_id',a.approval_id,'request_key',a.request_key,'plan_sha256',a.plan_sha256,'subset_sha256',a.subset_sha256,'contract_sha256',a.contract_sha256,'queue_manifest_sha256',a.queue_manifest_sha256,'batch_id',a.batch_id,'binding',a.binding,'binding_canonical_bytes',a.binding_canonical_bytes,'binding_sha256',a.binding_sha256,'server_commit_receipt',a.server_commit_receipt),'batch_identity',jsonb_build_object('batch_id',b.batch_id,'request_key',b.request_key,'source_kind',b.source_kind,'source_folder_id',b.source_folder_id,'output_folder_id',b.output_folder_id,'work_folder_id',b.work_folder_id,'processing_profile',b.processing_profile,'algorithm_revision',b.algorithm_revision,'inventory_sha256',b.inventory_sha256,'expected_count',b.expected_count,'total_size_bytes',b.total_size_bytes,'canary_source_file_id',b.canary_source_file_id,'result_mode',b.result_mode,'canonical_promotion_allowed',b.canonical_promotion_allowed,'database_persistence_allowed',b.database_persistence_allowed,'created_at',b.created_at),'jobs',(SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('job_id',j.job_id,'batch_id',j.batch_id,'source_file_id',j.source_file_id,'stable_job_key',j.stable_job_key,'sequence',j.sequence,'source_name',j.source_name,'source_mime_type',j.source_mime_type,'source_size_bytes',j.source_size_bytes,'source_checksum',j.source_checksum,'is_canary',j.is_canary,'created_at',j.created_at) ORDER BY j.sequence) FROM video_queue.job j WHERE j.batch_id=a.batch_id),'reservations',(SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('source_identity',r.source_identity,'admission_id',r.admission_id,'request_key',r.request_key,'source_fingerprint',r.source_fingerprint,'batch_id',r.batch_id,'job_id',r.job_id,'reservation_kind',r.reservation_kind,'historical_job_ids',r.historical_job_ids,'historical_provenance',r.historical_provenance) ORDER BY r.source_identity) FROM video_queue.source_reservation r WHERE r.admission_id=a.admission_id)) AS immutable_state FROM video_queue.subset_admission a JOIN video_queue.batch b USING(batch_id) WHERE a.request_key=$1::text;
immutable_snapshot.expected: JSONB-equal before/after recovery, worker transitions or rejected mutations. Includes full immutable queue-manifest identity/flags, actual batch/job mapping and approved fingerprints; excludes mutable status, leases, attempts, output, error, retry/updated/completed timestamps and authorization revocation state.

full_snapshot.sql: SELECT jsonb_build_object('batches',(SELECT coalesce(jsonb_agg(to_jsonb(b) ORDER BY b.batch_id),'[]'::jsonb) FROM video_queue.batch b WHERE b.request_key=ANY($1::text[])),'jobs',(SELECT coalesce(jsonb_agg(to_jsonb(j) ORDER BY j.job_id),'[]'::jsonb) FROM video_queue.job j JOIN video_queue.batch b USING(batch_id) WHERE b.request_key=ANY($1::text[])),'events',(SELECT coalesce(jsonb_agg(to_jsonb(e) ORDER BY e.event_id),'[]'::jsonb) FROM video_queue.job_event e JOIN video_queue.batch b USING(batch_id) WHERE b.request_key=ANY($1::text[])),'headers',(SELECT coalesce(jsonb_agg(to_jsonb(a) ORDER BY a.request_key),'[]'::jsonb) FROM video_queue.subset_admission a WHERE a.request_key=ANY($1::text[])),'reservations',(SELECT coalesce(jsonb_agg(to_jsonb(r) ORDER BY r.source_identity),'[]'::jsonb) FROM video_queue.source_reservation r WHERE r.source_identity=ANY($2::text[])),'observations',(SELECT coalesce(jsonb_agg(to_jsonb(o) ORDER BY o.observation_id),'[]'::jsonb) FROM video_queue.source_observation o WHERE o.request_key=ANY($1::text[]))) AS state;
full_snapshot.expected: JSONB-equal before/after rejected statements, including original source_observation rows and consumed_at/consumed_by_admission_id. Capture failure snapshot before issuing a replacement observation. PostgreSQL sequence allocations are excluded.

canary_only.sql: SELECT count(*) FILTER(WHERE j.is_canary AND j.status='QUEUED')=1 AND count(*) FILTER(WHERE NOT j.is_canary AND j.status='PENDING_CANARY')=count(*)-1 AS ok FROM video_queue.job j JOIN video_queue.batch b USING(batch_id) WHERE b.request_key=$1::text;

no_partial_loser.sql: SELECT NOT EXISTS(SELECT FROM video_queue.subset_admission WHERE request_key=$1::text) AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT FROM video_queue.batch WHERE request_key=$1::text) AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT FROM video_queue.source_reservation WHERE source_identity=ANY($2::text[])) AS ok;
parameters: loser-only source identities (exclude sources owned by winner)

no_fourth_attempt.sql: SELECT NOT EXISTS(SELECT FROM video_queue.job j JOIN video_queue.subset_admission a ON a.batch_id=j.batch_id WHERE j.attempt_count>3) AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT FROM video_queue.job_event e JOIN video_queue.job j ON j.job_id=e.job_id AND j.batch_id=e.batch_id JOIN video_queue.subset_admission a ON a.batch_id=j.batch_id WHERE e.event_type IN ('CLAIMED','RECLAIMED') AND (e.details->>'attempt')::integer>3) AS ok;
no_fourth_attempt.scope: Only jobs and events attached to managed subset_admission batches. Legacy historical jobs with >3 attempts may be preserved under HISTORICAL_HOLD tombstones; they must remain ineligible and are not a failure of this managed-attempt assertion.

zero_release.sql: SELECT b.status='CANARY_REVIEW' AND b.completed_at IS NULL AND (SELECT count(*) FROM video_queue.job j WHERE j.batch_id=b.batch_id AND NOT j.is_canary AND j.status='PENDING_CANARY')=b.expected_count-1 AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT FROM video_queue.job_event e WHERE e.batch_id=b.batch_id AND e.details->>'released_jobs' IS NOT NULL AND (e.details->>'released_jobs')::integer<>0) AS ok FROM video_queue.batch b WHERE b.request_key=$1::text;

permanent_reservations.sql: SELECT coalesce(jsonb_agg(to_jsonb(r) ORDER BY r.source_identity),'[]'::jsonb) = $2::jsonb AS ok FROM video_queue.source_reservation r WHERE r.source_identity=ANY($1::text[]);

no_partial_visibility.sql: SELECT NOT EXISTS(SELECT FROM video_queue.batch b WHERE b.request_key=$1::text) AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT FROM video_queue.subset_admission a WHERE a.request_key=$1::text) AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT FROM video_queue.source_reservation r WHERE r.source_identity=ANY($2::text[])) AS ok;
parameters: source identities with no prior committed history

observation_consumption_unchanged.sql: SELECT coalesce(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('observation_id',o.observation_id,'nonce',o.nonce,'consumed_at',o.consumed_at,'consumed_by_admission_id',o.consumed_by_admission_id) ORDER BY o.observation_id),'[]'::jsonb) AS observation_consumption FROM video_queue.source_observation o WHERE o.request_key=ANY($1::text[]);
